newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nail up on hope of Gold Fields stake.
newsitem.headline: Nail up on hope of Gold Fields stake.

text.p: Continuing hopes that black empowerment group New Africa Investments Ltd (Nail) might snatch a stake in Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd sprang Nail shares higher on Monday, dealers said.
Nail said earlier on Monday that talks with the mining house were continuing.
"Gold Fields is an absolute plum and there's a lot of competition to get it. As long as talks continue, the Nail shares will be buoyed," one dealer said.
By 1108 GMT Nail had added over five percent of its market value, rising 20 cents to 410 cents in a volume of 32,800 shares.
Last month Nail said it was in talks to buy an effective 17.2 percent stake in Gold Fields, giving it joint control with Rembrandt Group Ltd, which already owns a similar stake.
If successful, the deal would mark a further big advance for black business in South Africa and a significant coup for Nail which already has control of industrial group Johnnic.

Discussions also involve Gold Fields jewel mine Driefontein Consolidated Ltd. Nail is negotiating to acquire Gold Fields and Dries' shareholdings in Asteroid Ltd, which holds 40 percent of Gold Fields of South Africa Holdings Ltd.
This would translate into the effective 17.2 percent stake in Gold Fields.
But dealers cautioned that Nail would need assistance to acquire any stake in Gold Fields or Dries.

"Look at their market caps. It's a David and Goliath story here. There's only one way that Nail can get a meaningful stake and thats if they get help and it's given to them on a plate. But the fact that talks are going on is a promising sign," a dealer said.
Nail's market cap is around 320 million rand, while Gold Fields is about 10 billion rand and Dries about six billion rand, dealers said.
Dries shares fell over two percent on Monday to 30.90 rand, a new year low, with 50,400 shares changing hands.
But dealers said all gold stocks on the JSE were taking a knock as bullion struggled to escape low levels.

The gold price was last bid at $334.10 an ounce -- a 52-month low -- dragging the South African all-gold index to its lowest level since March 1993. The index was last 967.5 points, 27.3 points down on the day.
"All the gold shares are down today," a dealer said.
Gold Fields was steady at 107.50 rand in meagre volume of 5,500 shares.
